review_notes: I read the whole target file. I checked Mathlib's Algebra/Polynomial/Bivariate.lean (equivMvPolynomial, Bivariate.swap, aevalAeval, aevalAeval_swap). I also checked the project's transposeBivariate (BivariateResultant.lean) and evalBivariate (AuxiliaryFamily.lean). frobeniusSubfield comes from Mathlib or a dependency rather than being defined here. perfectConstantsToFrobeniusSubfield is a codRestrict wrapper, which I judged a legitimate small wrapper. I did not read the bodies of the downstream resultant lemmas, so I can't say how much of them would need to change under the proposed migrations. Neither migration has been compiled.

findings.problem: This builds a second equivalence between K[X0,X1] and K[X][Y] by chaining finSuccEquiv, mapAlgEquiv and uniqueAlgEquiv. Mathlib already has Polynomial.Bivariate.equivMvPolynomial R : R[X][Y] ≃ₐ[R] MvPolynomial (Fin 2) R, and Polynomial.Bivariate.swap exchanges the two variables. The file's own theorem transposeBivariate_planeCurveToBivariate shows planeCurveToBivariate is the Mathlib equivalence followed by a swap. The only difference is orientation. This orientation is why the file needs bespoke X_zero, X_one and C simp lemmas, a natDegree-vs-degreeOf proof, and a transposition-compatibility proof.
findings.proposed_change: Define it as `(Polynomial.Bivariate.equivMvPolynomial K).symm.trans Polynomial.Bivariate.swap`, which has the same type. The X_zero, X_one and C lemmas should follow from Bivariate.swap_X, swap_Y, swap_C_C, equivMvPolynomial_symm_X_0, equivMvPolynomial_symm_X_1 and equivMvPolynomial_symm_C. transposeBivariate_planeCurveToBivariate then becomes a statement about swap versus the project's transposeBivariate. The existing proof of bivariateEquiv_symm_natDegree_eq_degreeOf_one can be reused for the second degree. Alternatively, work with Mathlib's orientation throughout.
findings.benefit: This removes a parallel finSuccEquiv-based equivalence and about 70 lines of generator-chasing proofs (lines 51–147). It also lets Mathlib's swap and aevalAeval_swap lemmas apply directly.

findings.problem: This file leans on the project-local evalBivariate (P.eval₂ (eval₂RingHom (algebraMap C L) u) v) and transposeBivariate (eval₂RingHom with mapRingHom C and C X), which is exactly Mathlib's swap on C[X][Y]. Mathlib's Polynomial.aevalAeval x y evaluates an element of R[X][Y] at an inner point x and an outer point y over an algebra A. Mathlib also has Bivariate.swap and Bivariate.aevalAeval_swap (aevalAeval x y (swap p) = aevalAeval y x p). So both concepts exist, and the lemma proved here (evaluation after base change agrees with MvPolynomial.eval₂) is reproved by a long ringHom_ext argument.
findings.proposed_change: Restate evalBivariate u v P as Mathlib's aevalAeval u v P, which needs the appropriate Algebra instances. Alternatively, prove that the two agree and use Mathlib's aevalAeval lemmas. Replace transposeBivariate by Polynomial.Bivariate.swap, adapting transposeBivariate_coeff_natDegree_le and the transpose_transpose lemma to use swap_swap_apply.
findings.benefit: Downstream proofs can reuse Mathlib's simp set for aevalAeval and swap. The project stops maintaining a duplicate evaluation and transposition API, and hgZero and the degree bookkeeping become shorter.
